ABAKADA Party-List

HOW TO FAST-TRACK AID  TO ‘LANDO’  VICTIMS!
It was only typhoon ‘Lando’s” first day yesterday but the devastation already appears to be widespread.

Recorded evacuees included 4,000 families or at least 16,000 people in 11 towns and two cities in Isabela, 3,003 families or 10,167 people in Aurora and over 3,000 in Nueva Ecija. Evacuations were also reported in Ilocos Sur, Pangasinan, Zambales, Bulacan, Benguet and Kalinga. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) reported sections of 24 roads and 10 bridges in Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Bicol and the CAR were not passable because of landslides and floods. The roads included the Baler-Casiguran Road and the Dinadiawan-Madella Road in Aurora. The Manila Electric Co. reported that about 130,000 of its customers, suffered power outages, with Cavite and Rizal as the hardest hit. Power failures were also reported in San Fernando City in La Union and in 18 towns in the Ilocos region and Central and southern Luzon. The Philippine Coast Guard monitored as many as 5,580 passengers, 78 vessels, 45 motorized bancas and 537 rolling cargoes stranded. 

We, therefore, strongly urge the DSWD to use without delay all available Philippine Air Force and Philippine Navy planes and ships to fast-track the delivery of immediate needs of evacuees like food.  We call on the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to work 24 hours a day in clearing all blocked roads and bridges. If necessary, they should hire extra laborers or reassign personnel from other areas to clearing sites. Bureaucratic red tape should be reduced for faster release of funds for immediate basic needs of ‘Lando’ victims. Residents of affected areas must join hands with local government officials and personnel in caring for evacuees and in removing debris. And to further ensure speedy assistance to the victims, we hope President Aquino will take a direct hand in all relief efforts.

Time is of the essence for ‘Lando’’ victims. 30
